mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < 500k) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 500k in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises above its 12-month moving average signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when inflation is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.6% signals a deflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered deflationary months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a precautionary savings behavior, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.4% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains unchanged or rises signals a mismatch between job creation and labor force participation, which typically precedes a slowdown in consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.3% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
